Export an interactive dichotomous key

Source: R/export.R
exportWizard.Rd

Writes a dimoose key as a single self-contained HTML page. With JavaScript on, the page steps through the key one couplet at a time, keeps a trail of the choices made (each one clickable to go back to it) and supports the browser's Back button. Without JavaScript, the same page is the full key with every lead hyperlinked to its next couplet or taxon. Each taxon gets a result section listing the characters on its path, and a map of the key shows where the user is (see map).

Usage

exportWizard(
  key = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  displayLinks = TRUE,
  order = "original",
  title = NULL,
  map = TRUE,
  staticPaths = NULL,
  matrix = NULL,
  characters = NULL,
  taxon = "Taxon",
  offline = FALSE,
  photoModel = NULL,
  photoRuntime = NULL
)

Arguments

key

A dimoose object, e.g. from importFishbase(). May be NULL if matrix is given.

file

Path of the HTML file to write. If NULL, the HTML is returned as a string instead.

displayLinks

If TRUE, show the couplet numbers each lead leads to and comes from, as in a printed key. If FALSE, hide them. Leads stay clickable either way.

order

Deprecated and ignored. Couplets are always exported in the key's own order. "parsimony" was never implemented; to ask the questions that are easiest to observe first, build the key with keyFromMatrix() and give the characters a Cost.

title

Page title. Defaults to the key's description.

map

If TRUE, include a map of the key: the whole key drawn as a tree, marking the current couplet, the path taken so far and the branches (and number of taxa) still possible. It sits beside the key on wide screens and behind a Map button on phones.

staticPaths

If TRUE, write each taxon's path through the key into the page, so it shows without JavaScript. If FALSE, the page builds the path in the browser when a result is shown, which keeps large keys (such as phylotreeKey() on the whole tree) much smaller. The default is TRUE for keys with up to 1,000 taxa.

matrix

Optional character matrix: a data frame with one row per taxon, the taxon's name in column taxon and one column per character. Cells are states; several states of one taxon are separated by "/"; NA is unknown or inapplicable. See 'Picking characters in any order'.

characters

Optional data frame describing the characters of matrix: column Character (a column name of matrix) and any of Cost (lower is easier to observe), Season (when it can be observed) and Needs (e.g. "hand lens").

taxon

Name of the column of matrix that holds the taxon names.

offline

If TRUE, also write a web app manifest, a service worker and icons next to file, so that the page can be installed and opened without a connection. Needs file. See 'Offline use'.

photoModel

Optional: a folder written by exportBrowserModel() for this key, or the web address (https://...) of one. Adds "Identify from a photo" to the page. See 'Identifying from a photo'.

photoRuntime

Optional web address of a folder holding the dist files of onnxruntime-web (ort.wasm.min.js, ort-wasm-simd-threaded.mjs and .wasm), to serve them yourself instead of loading them from jsDelivr. Relative addresses are relative to the page.

Value

The path to file, invisibly, or the HTML as a character string if file is NULL. With offline = TRUE or a photoModel folder the paths of the other files written are in attribute "files".

Details

The key is checked first: leads pointing at missing couplets, terminal leads without a taxon, couplets with fewer than two leads and couplets that cannot be reached from the first one are reported as warnings and marked in the page.

Not sure

Every couplet has an "I'm not sure" button (keys u or ?). It follows all leads of the couplet at once. The page then asks the questions of one branch at a time, lists the branches still open (click one to answer it next), and counts and marks on the map the taxa possible in any of them. Each answer narrows its own branch. If the reader stays unsure to the end, the page lists every result that is left. Back undoes one step at a time. The address of the page records the open branches (#open=c-3,c-9), so a reload or a shared link returns to the same place; the trail of choices comes back too when the browser restores the page's history entry.

Picking characters in any order

With matrix, the page gains a second way in: a list of the characters of the matrix, to answer in any order. Picking a state removes the taxa that do not have it. A taxon with several states ("a/b") fits any of them, and a taxon whose state is unknown (NA) fits all. The characters that still separate the remaining taxa are listed first: cheapest first when characters gives a Cost, then those that leave the fewest taxa on average. Taxa of the matrix are matched to the key's taxa by name (ignoring case), so the remaining taxa link to their result sections and show on the map, and the page offers to continue step by step from the couplet they all share. Without JavaScript the matrix is a plain table. The two ways are otherwise independent: answers given step by step do not filter the character list. With key = NULL the page is the character list alone.

Offline use

The page itself needs no connection once it is open, but a browser will not reopen a page it cannot fetch. offline = TRUE writes four files next to file, named after it: a web app manifest (<name>.webmanifest), a service worker (<name>-sw.js) and two icons (<name>-icon-192.png, <name>-icon-512.png; the package logo if the rsvg package is installed, otherwise a simple drawn icon). The worker stores the page, the manifest, the icons and the figures the page loads from other sites, so that the page can be installed on a phone ("Add to Home Screen") and opened without signal. Upload all five files to the same folder. Limits:

  • Browsers run service workers only on https:// or http://localhost. A page opened from disk (file://) works as before but is not installed and stores nothing.

  • The page must be opened once with a connection before it works without.

  • Figures on other sites are fetched when the worker installs and again when first shown; any that fail are skipped. A site that does not allow cross-origin requests gives an opaque copy, which browsers count as several megabytes each against the storage they allow, so a key with many such figures may not store them all. Figures embedded in the key (see imageMeta()) are part of the page and always available. Full-size figures and taxon pages that open in a new tab are not stored.

  • The worker only controls the page it was written for (its scope is the page's own address), so several keys can share a folder. Serve the page under its file name; a server that drops the .html from addresses puts the page outside the worker's scope.

Identifying from a photo

photoModel adds an "Identify from a photo" button. The reader takes or picks a photo; the page loads the model and onnxruntime-web (the program that runs it, version 1.31.1, about 15 MB, from the jsDelivr CDN unless photoRuntime says otherwise), prepares the picture as the model's model.json says, runs the image encoder in the browser and compares the result with the text embeddings of the key's taxa. The photo never leaves the reader's device. The page then marks the likely taxa on the map, lists the five best with their scores, each linked to its result, and offers to narrow the key to them: the leads that reach none of them are greyed and the count of remaining taxa follows, but every lead still works. The key stays the authority; the photo is a hint.

photoModel is a folder written by exportBrowserModel() for the same key, or the web address of one. The model is not put into the page. A folder is copied next to file as <name>_model/ (so file is needed); upload it with the page. A web address is used as it is; a model on another site must allow cross-origin requests. What to expect:

  • Nothing is downloaded until the reader has chosen a photo, been told the size and agreed. An int8 BioCLIP encoder is 90 MB; with the runtime that is about 105 MB on first use. The page shows the progress.

  • With offline = TRUE the service worker keeps the model and the runtime once they have been fetched, so photos can be identified without a connection afterwards. That is the same 105 MB or so of storage on the reader's device, and the first use still needs a connection.

  • It needs a browser with WebAssembly, and memory: several times the size of the encoder while it loads. If the browser cannot run the model, runs out of memory or cannot fetch it, the page says so and the key works as before. A page opened from disk (file://) cannot load the model.

  • Only the WebAssembly backend is used, on one thread unless the page is served cross-origin isolated. That suits int8 encoders, which WebGPU cannot run.

  • The scores compare the key's taxa with each other and add up to 100%, so a photo of something that is not in the key still gets a confident best match. If model.json has a min_similarity, a best match whose cosine similarity is under it is shown as "Not much like any taxon of this key" without a percentage.

Notes on leads

A Note column in the key's leads, as pruneKey() writes when it collapses a couplet (the character of the couplet that is no longer asked), is shown under its lead as "Also:" and in the path of each result. A pruned_note in the key's meta (the same for a collapsed first couplet) is shown under the title.

Hook for other scripts

The page defines window.dimoose so that another script, for example one that identifies a photo in the browser, can work with the page without knowing how it is built:

  • dimoose.taxa: array of { id, name }, one per result.

  • dimoose.highlight(scores, opts): scores is an object mapping taxon names or ids to numbers, or an array of { taxon, score }; null clears. Marks those taxa on the map and in every list of candidates and lists the five best above the key, headed by opts.label (default "Suggested"). Scores all within 0 to 1 are shown as percentages. Returns the ids it marked, best first.

  • dimoose.goToTaxon(nameOrId): shows that result; false if unknown.

  • dimoose.narrow(namesOrIds): narrows the key to these taxa (see 'Identifying from a photo'); null undoes it. Returns the ids kept.

  • dimoose.state(): { shown, open, remaining, picks, narrowed }, the section shown, the open branches, the ids of the taxa still possible, the states picked in the character list and the ids the key is narrowed to (or null).

  • dimoose.photo (only with photoModel): identify(file), a promise of the ranked taxa, and the pure steps preprocess() and score().

  • dimoose.onChange(fn): calls fn(state) after every step.

See also

keyFromMatrix() to build a key from a character matrix.

Examples

leads <- data.frame(
  Statement = c("1", "1", "2", "2"), Choice = c("a", "b", "a", "b"),
  Character = c("Wings present", "Wings absent", "Two wings", "Four wings"),
  Next = c("2", "-", "-", "-"), Taxon = c("", "Silverfish", "Fly", "Bee")
)
key <- keyFromLeads(leads, "A tiny key")
html <- exportWizard(key)
substr(html, 1, 15)
#> [1] "<!doctype html>"

# With a character matrix the reader can also pick characters in any order
insects <- data.frame(
  Taxon = c("Silverfish", "Fly", "Bee", "Ant"),
  Wings = c("absent", "present", "present", "present/absent"),
  Sting = c("absent", "absent", "present", NA)
)
characters <- data.frame(Character = c("Wings", "Sting"), Cost = c(1, 3),
                         Needs = c("", "hand lens"))
html <- exportWizard(key, matrix = insects, characters = characters)
#> 1 of 4 taxa of the matrix are not results of the key and get no link: Ant

# A matrix alone makes a page with only the character list
html <- exportWizard(NULL, matrix = insects, title = "Four insects")

# An installable copy that opens without a connection once it is served
# over https: the page, a manifest, a service worker and two icons
dir <- tempfile("key")
dir.create(dir)
out <- exportWizard(key, file.path(dir, "insects.html"), offline = TRUE)
list.files(dir)
#> [1] "insects-icon-192.png" "insects-icon-512.png" "insects-sw.js"       
#> [4] "insects.html"         "insects.webmanifest" 
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
